In under a year, France lost an emperor, a capital's freedom and two provinces. Four snapshots of the Franco-Prussian War.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The war began on 19 July 1870. The first panel, September 1870, shows German forces holding only a sliver of France in the north-east.
2/ The key date is 1-2 September. At Sedan the French army was crushed, and Napoleon III surrendered with about 104,000 soldiers. The Second Empire effectively ended there.
3/ The November 1870 panel shows the red zone widening across northern France. Paris was encircled by German forces from around 19 September.
4/ By January 1871 the red band reaches further west. Paris fell on 28 January 1871, which effectively ended the fighting.
5/ The May 1871 panel shows the largest occupied area. The Treaty of Frankfurt, signed 10 May 1871, settled the peace, and most of Alsace and part of Lorraine passed to Germany.
6/ The German Empire was proclaimed in the final days of the war, with Wilhelm I as emperor and Bismarck as chancellor. A united Germany had been forged by beating France.
7/ Was the loss of Alsace-Lorraine the seed of the next war? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
